text:
Hello Sarah — good to meet you. I'm **sarah-agent**, a *bia*: an assistant that lives on this computer. Its disks, files and accounts are mine to look after, and I'm here to work for you.

- **Web app** — from a phone or computer on the same network, open https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca). The first visit lets you take the root certificate; after that you have chats with me, files, the screen and voice right there.
- **My own messaging accounts** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts so you can write and call me there, plus my own Messenger and Instagram. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number (not yours): you create it in the app on a phone with that number, then scan a QR code to log me in. Want me to set any of those up?
- **My own accounts online** — I can sign up for websites and services (e-mail and others) in my own browser, keep the passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you for help when a captcha or a phone check comes up.
- **And more** — I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and talk with you by voice.

I've also read your briefing: I'm your teaching assistant for CSE455 (Prof. Alvarez), and I'll keep `/home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md` up to date — bookings, declines and deletions logged under `## Log` — and stick to working hours, Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00.

What would you like to start with?

Hello — I'm **alvarez-agent**, the bia that lives on this machine (bia). I manage Professor Alvarez's calendar and messages for CSE455.

I've read the briefing: working hours Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00, the schedule in `/home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md` with a change log, and I can write to contacts here on the web channel.

A couple of things about me, in one line each:
- **Web app** (https://127.0.0.1:8443, CA https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): from a phone or computer on this network you can take the root certificate and get chats, files, the screen and voice with me.
- **My own messaging accounts**: I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp, MAX, Messenger and Instagram — each needs a separate account with its own phone number (you create it and scan a QR to log me in). Say the word if you want that.
- **My own online accounts**: I can register on websites and services in my own browser and keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store, asking you when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- **Also**: I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and talk by voice.

Ready. What should I start with — anything already on the calendar, or a message for Sarah?

On it. Professor Alvarez's next week (Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov) is packed; the only free half-hour windows are:

- Mon 10:00–10:30, Mon 14:00–14:30
- Tue 11:00–11:30, Tue 15:00–15:30
- Wed 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30

I've messaged Sarah to ask which of those work for her. Shall I book 30 minutes, or would you like it longer — and is there anything I should put in the invite?

Understood — I'll handle it. My plan: a 30-minute staff meeting, first choice **Mon 23 Nov 14:00–14:30**, fallback Mon 10:00–10:30 / Tue 11:00–11:30. I'll book once Sarah confirms a slot, log it in CALENDAR.md and tell her. No need to answer.

Done: CSE455 staff meeting booked **Wed 23 Nov, 10:00–10:30** with Sarah (her easiest slot too), added to the Wednesday section of CALENDAR.md and logged as `BOOKED: Wednesday 10:00-10:30 with Sarah`. Sarah is confirming on her side.
